[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested that companies can ensure their wellness programs are inclusive by conducting a needs assessment, being culturally sensitive, promoting unbiased participation, ensuring accessibility, offering language options, and providing flexibility.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided examples of inclusive wellness program initiatives, including on-demand sessions, virtual programs, health and wellness fairs, support groups, and interpreter services.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant offered tips to motivate employees to participate in wellness programs, such as making the program fun, offering incentives, setting goals, leveraging peer support, communicating effectively, offering flexibility, and measuring progress.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant emphasized the importance of setting SMART goals (specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and time-bound) for wellness programs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided examples of SMART wellness goals, such as losing five pounds in two months, participating in mindfulness sessions, and walking 10,000 steps a day.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant discussed the benefits of offering incentives, including healthy office snacks, to motivate participation in wellness programs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant highlighted that providing healthy snacks can create a culture around healthy eating habits and foster community among employees.
